prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
A curious gap is opening in how young people in Japan think about travel.

Their wishes are becoming more personal. Especially among young men, travelers want to choose their own pace, follow their interests, and leave more of the day open.

Several surveys point in this direction. In a 2025 survey, men aged 29 or under placed solo travel at about 25% among their preferred travel styles. Hobby-focused travel showed the same pattern.

Another survey found an even stronger wish for freedom. About 90% of Japanese Gen Z travelers with overseas travel experience wanted free time during a tour. About 80% wanted at least half a day.

But here is the twist.

When people were asked what they would do if they could take a full month off, the most common answer was a trip of about one week. It was chosen by about 24% of respondents.

In a separate autumn survey of people planning a trip, the expected stay was much shorter: an average of 1.8 nights and a median of 2 nights.

So the story is not that young Japanese travelers have already moved completely from famous sights to long, slow stays. The stronger signal is in their wishes. Their idea of a good trip is becoming more self-directed, while the time they plan to spend away remains limited.

A national tourism white paper also lists longer stays as a policy task. That suggests the change is still developing, rather than already complete.

【Point One】
The useful distinction is between duration and pace. A short trip can still give travelers control: one personal interest, a solo plan, or a half-day block without fixed activities. For travel businesses, the opportunity may be to change the shape of short trips, not only to sell longer packages.

【Point Two】
Japan’s young travelers are not moving as one group. Women aged 29 or under still show strong interest in gourmet travel, at about 52%, and famous tourist spots, at about 45%. Men lean more toward solo and hobby-led trips. Destinations may need different ways to experience the same place.

point_one.reasoning: 旅行期間の長短と、旅行中に自分で過ごし方を決められる自由度を区別し、短期旅行でも半日単位の自由時間や趣味中心の設計が可能だという具体的な示唆を加えている。単なる本文の言い換えではなく、旅行事業者が短期商品の構成を見直すという実務的含意も示している。

point_two.reasoning: 若年層を一括りにせず、29歳以下の女性のグルメ・有名観光地志向と男性の一人旅・趣味志向を具体的な数値で対比している。これにより、同じ目的地でも性別や関心に応じて異なる体験設計が必要だという新しい示唆が得られる。
